items.q: Under the treatment heading, the holistic approach to CKD is:
items.exp: Treatment: KDIGO 23; holistic approach to CKD: first line. (Book p807)

items.q: The lifestyle block recommends salt restriction of:
items.exp: Lifestyle: healthy diet — salt restriction (2-3 g/day). (Book p807)

items.q: Risk-factor reassessment in the lifestyle block is recommended every:
items.exp: Lifestyle: risk factor reassessment (every 3-6 months). (Book p807)

items.q: Match the following lifestyle item to its detail — 1) Diet  2) Tobacco  3) Weight … A) Stop use of products  B) Salt restriction 2-3 g/day  C) Management
items.exp: Lifestyle: healthy diet (salt restriction 2-3 g/day); physical activity; stop use of tobacco products; weight management; risk factor reassessment every 3-6 months. (Book p807)

opts: ACE(-)/ARBs plus SGLT2 inhibitors (curb the fall in GFR)
Loop diuretics — for volume overload control
Calcium channel blockers — for BP control only
items.exp: Manage proteinuria: 1st line — ACE(-)/ARBs, SGLT2 (curb ↓ in GFR). (Book p807)

items.q: The second-line agent for proteinuria, written in red, is:
The BP target for CKD in the first-line table is:
items.exp: BP control: <120/80 mmHg — 24-hr ambulatory monitoring. (Book p807)

items.q: Fill up: BP control in the table uses ACE(-)/ARBs or ______, which must not be combined with ACE(-)/ARB.
items.exp: BP control: ACE(-)/ARBs or aliskiren (do not combine with ACE(-)/ARB). (Book p807)

items.q: All but one are listed for BP control in the first-line table. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: BP control: ACE(-)/ARBs or aliskiren; non-dihydropyridine CCBs. Finerenone is the 2nd-line proteinuria agent. (Book p807)

items.q: For LDL control (<100 mg/dl), the statin-based therapy named is:
items.exp: LDL control <100 mg/dl — statin based therapy: rosuvastatin 20 mg/kg. (Book p807)

items.q: Match the following LDL target to its group — 1) CKD  2) Diabetic CKD  3) Diabetic CKD with previous cardiovascular event … A) 70 mg/dl  B) 100 mg/dl  C) 55 mg/dl
items.exp: LDL targets: CKD 100 mg/dl; diabetic CKD 70 mg/dl; diabetic CKD with previous cardiovascular event 55 mg/dl. (Book p807)

items.q: Which set lists the contraindications for ACE(-)s written on the page?
opts: Pregnancy, B/L or unilateral renal artery stenosis, Cr rise >30% or K+ >5.5 mg/dl after starting, hereditary angioedema
Pregnancy, GFR below 30 ml/min, uncontrolled diabetes, resistant hypertension
Unilateral renal vein thrombosis, hypokalemia, gout and hereditary angioedema
Pregnancy, bilateral pulmonary fibrosis, hyperkalemia before starting and asthma
items.exp: C/I for ACE(-)s: pregnancy; B/L or unilateral renal artery stenosis; if s. Cr ↑ >30%, s. K+ ↑ >5.5 mg/dl after starting Rx; hereditary angioedema. (Book p807)

items.q: An ACE inhibitor must be reviewed if, after starting, the serum creatinine rises by more than:
items.exp: C/I if s. Cr ↑ >30% (or s. K+ ↑ >5.5 mg/dl) after starting Rx. (Book p807)

items.q: Bilateral renal artery stenosis is listed as a contraindication for ACE(-)s.
opts: False — only unilateral stenosis is listed
False — stenosis is a relative indication
True, but only in diabetic patients
items.exp: C/I for ACE(-)s includes B/L or unilateral renal artery stenosis. (Book p807)

items.q: A CKD patient with type 2 diabetes and a previous myocardial infarction needs an LDL target. The target is:
items.exp: LDL targets: diabetic CKD with previous cardiovascular event — 55 mg/dl. (Book p807)

items.q: SGLT2 inhibitors are included in first-line proteinuria management and they curb the fall in GFR.
items.exp: 1st line: ACE(-)/ARBs, SGLT2 (curb ↓ in GFR). (Book p807)
